question: Who appoints the Attorney-General of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Attorney General is a part of the Union Executive.
 
• He is the highest law officer in the country.
 
• Article 76 provides for the Attorney General of India, hence it is a constitutional office.
 
• His term is not fixed by the constitution and he works at the pleasure of the President.
 
• Functions-
 
 
• To advise, the government upon such legal matters, referred by the President.
 
• To appear on behalf of the GoI in all cases in the Supreme Court or in the High Court.
 
• To represent the GoI in any reference made by the President to the Supreme Court under Article 143.
 
• To discharge the functions conferred on him by the constitution or any other law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• He can take part in proceedings of both the Houses of Parliament but can't vote.
 
• He enjoys the same privileges and immunities as enjoyed by members of parliament.
 
• He does not fall into the category of government servants.
 
• He is assisted by the Solicitor Generals of India.
